summary: Split-DNS views + ECMP path selection causing intermittent service discovery flapping in private deployment
description: Customer reports intermittent failures where agent instances in their private deployment fail to resolve control-plane hostnames or resolve to different IPs that intermittently reject TLS handshakes. Symptoms began after a recent network change (added a second transit attachment and enabled ECMP for egress). Failures cause model pulls to fail and gRPC streams to drop for bursts of ~30-90s before recovering.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) From a node in the customer's private subnet run: dig +short control-api.internal.finedge
2) Repeat the dig command several times in quick succession and note alternating A records
3) curl -v --resolve control-api.internal.finedge:443:<ip_from_dig> https://control-api.internal.finedge/health
4) Observe TLS certificate common name and occasional connection resets when dig returns alternate IP
5) Reproduce from multiple AZs/subnets to see AZ-correlated behaviour.
logs:
Customer-provided dig/tcpdump snippets: 
- dig outputs: 10.0.5.21
10.0.8.42
10.0.5.21
- tcpdump on node: DNS requests (udp/53) source=10.0.5.50 -> 172.31.2.10 and -> 172.31.3.11 (alternating)
- openssl s_client -connect 10.0.8.42:443 shows certificate CN=control-api.external.redwood.ai (mismatch)
- kube-agent logs: "x509: certificate is valid for control-api.private.redwood, not control-api.external.redwood.ai"
- Control plane logs show successful connection attempts from IPs in resolver-1 subnet and rejected/handshakes-from resolver-2 subnet
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: split-horizon DNS (resolver sets in two AZs) returns different record sets (one view returns private IPs tied to internal LB with private cert, the other returns an internal CNAME that resolves to an external-facing IP/hostname that presents external TLS cert). Enabling ECMP for egress caused packet flows to be hashed across two NAT paths which send DNS queries to different forwarders / resolvers based on path. Result: same client sometimes gets IP A, sometimes B within TTL window => TLS mismatch when client picks IP with external cert.
What we did: 
- Pulled route tables and observed two active NAT gateway paths with equal-cost routes for 0.0.0.0/0 and DNS traffic to resolver endpoints flowed to different forwarders depending on ECMP hash.
- Captured tcpdump showing DNS queries from same source to two different resolver IPs within 5s.
- Compared resolver responses: resolver-A returns 10.0.5.21 with cert CN control-api.private.redwood; resolver-B returns a CNAME that ultimately resolves to 34.x.y.z (external) with cert CN control-api.external.redwood.ai.
- Reproduced by temporarily forcing egress to a single path: DNS responses stabilized and TLS handshakes succeeded consistently.

resolution:
Mitigation validated: customer changed route preference to pin DNS egress to resolver-A (single path) and restarted agents on nodes. After change, DNS responses stabilized to the private-only view and TLS handshake failures stopped. Root cause: ECMP-induced path selection caused DNS queries to hit two different forwarders with inconsistent split-horizon views.
Permanent fix planned: customer will (a) reconfigure forwarders so both present identical internal views, and (b) update network design to avoid ECMP across resolvers for control-plane traffic. Redwood SRE to add documentation guidance for Private deployments about resolver consistency and ECMP pitfalls.
